target_customer: Bars, pubs, restaurants and hotels in the Netherlands and Europe
problem: Hospitality venues lose staff time and revenue taking table orders by hand, and menus are hard to change. Orderli lets guests scan a QR code, order and pay without an app.
business_model: B2B SaaS fixed monthly fee per venue with payment fees only for online payments
product_category: QR table ordering and payments for hospitality

founders.name: Dorus van den Oord
education: Delft University of Technology, Strategic Product Design
founders.background_notes: YC page: self taught front end developer.

founders.name: Maurits Franken
founders.background_notes: YC page: previously sold lottery tickets near train stations and cider to restaurants.

founders.name: Sven van der Zee
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder by Silicon Canals (Feb 2023) but not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web based menu, ordering and payments product integrated with POS systems. Integration breadth is the main effort.

defensibility.rationale: QR ordering was widely copyable during the pandemic. POS integrations and payment flows add some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Other QR ordering vendors were active in the Netherlands as of the later sources found. No source shows an acquisition of Orderli.

market_need_then: Tech.eu (Aug 2021) says Orderli acquired the venue check-in app mycapa.city, which had over 650 locations, reflecting pandemic rules. NL Times (Sept 2021) reported QR menus used to combat hospitality staff shortages.

identity.logo: Orange logo file (orderli-logo-oranje.svg) on the company site
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, warm and practical, with slogans such as 'Less running. More hospitality.' The mission cites making hospitality gezellig (Bouncewatch).

brand_strength.rationale: Clear warm voice but no press about the brand and a similar name to Orderlion and Orderly in search results.

outcome_analysis: Orderli is a small Dutch QR ordering company that joined YC in Summer 2021 after four earlier rejections per a Dutch trade report. It acquired a check-in app in August 2021, raised 875K in February 2023 at a reported valuation of 9M, and remains active with a small team. No acquisition, layoffs or shutdown were found. Its fate depends on competing with POS vendors and other QR players.
